caption: SemBind-Audio pipeline architecture (conceptual schematic of the frozen implementation).
interpretation: End-to-end flow: STFT -> HuBERT -> contribution Delta -> S/P/J -> coordinate selection -> adaptive delta -> bipolar embedding -> ISTFT -> reference-based extraction -> majority vote -> SHA-256 verification.
caveat: Conceptual diagram (allowed); not an experimental plot and makes no performance claim.

caption: Actual embedding locations (red dots) over log-magnitude spectrograms for three real recordings.
interpretation: Selected (frequency_bin,time_frame) coordinates spread across the eligible band and timeline via the frozen joint-suitability allocation.
caveat: Diagnostic run on 3 files only using frozen methodology; illustrative, NOT a corpus statistic. Per-coordinate data was not persisted in E1-E14.

caption: Per-frame semantic suitability S, spectral suitability P, and joint suitability J for three real recordings.
interpretation: Shows how S, P, and their multiplicative combination J vary over time.
caveat: Diagnostic run on 3 files only; illustrative, NOT a corpus statistic.

caption: Payload success (%) vs replica redundancy R=1,2,3 (n=500 each).
interpretation: R=3 reaches 100% clean recovery; R=1 99.60%, R=2 99.40%.
caveat: Non-monotonic: R=2 is lower than R=1; do NOT claim more redundancy always improves performance.

caption: Mean bit error rate vs replica redundancy R=1,2,3 (n=500 each).
interpretation: BER falls to exactly 0 at R=3 (0.000094 at R=1, 0.000609 at R=2).

caption: Mean clean SNR vs replica redundancy R=1,2,3 (n=500 each).
interpretation: SNR decreases as R increases (78.89, 76.46, 74.82 dB) because more coordinates carry the same payload.
caveat: SNR reduction is the price of redundancy; not a defect.

caption: Recovery-quality trade-off: payload success vs mean clean SNR for R=1,2,3.
interpretation: R=3 trades ~4 dB SNR for a zero-failure clean payload recovery.
caveat: R=3 selected as final config; do NOT claim universally optimal.

caption: Mean clean SNR vs semantic weight alpha (beta = 1-alpha), n=500 each.
interpretation: Mean SNR increases monotonically from alpha=1.0 (72.75 dB) toward alpha=0.0 (76.63 dB).
caveat: All settings achieve 100% clean recovery; final config alpha=0.70.

caption: Mean clean SNR vs constant embedding strength delta (log scale), n=500 each.
interpretation: SNR decreases monotonically with delta (93.87 dB at 0.0005 -> 68.27 dB at 0.010).
caveat: Clean recovery is 100% across the tested range.

caption: Mean clean SNR by selection strategy (n=500 each).
interpretation: Spectral-only > joint > random > semantic-only in clean SNR; joint beats random by 1.12 dB.
caveat: Do NOT claim joint gives best SNR (spectral-only is higher); do NOT claim semantic-only best.

caption: Mean clean SNR by recording-duration bin (all 2620 recordings).
interpretation: SNR rises with duration from 72.54 dB (<4 s) to 80.71 dB (>20 s).

caption: Bit accuracy under AWGN (left) and common attacks (right), chance line at 50%; n=500 per attack.
interpretation: Bit accuracy collapses to 0.50-0.79; payload success is 0 under every attack.
caveat: The snr_db field in E9/E10 is PRE-attack embedding SNR and must not be shown as attack quality.

caption: Per-speaker mean clean SNR (40 speakers, all 2620 recordings).
interpretation: All 40 speakers achieve 100% payload recovery (worst-speaker success = 1.0).
caveat: Speaker IDs shown as LibriSpeech speaker numbers.

caption: Paired Cohen's dz effect sizes for clean SNR across method pairs (n=2620).
interpretation: All paired SNR differences are large (|dz| 1.41-4.18).
caveat: Statistical significance != practical/perceptual superiority; no perceptual metric measured.
